name: Siemens

Software Engineer / Graduate Engineer Tr.dsaDepth: Light–Moderate — resume-driven and fundamentals-first: OOP, core language behavior, simple DSA and SQL, with real depth expected on whatever technology you list, but rarely hard algorithms
rounds: Online assessment: 2-3 sections (technical MCQs, coding, sometimes aptitude/quant)

Technical interview(s) (1-2): OOP pillars explained with examples (C++ or Java), simple-to-medium DSA (linked list, array, pattern-printing, "find the unique word in a document"-style problems), and stack-specific depth for Java roles (multithreading, collections, Spring/Hibernate, SQL, JUnit/Mockito)
Managerial round: mostly behavioral, project discussion, "where do you see yourself in 5 years"
HR round: culture fit, logistics, salary
extraTopics: Explaining OOP concepts and design-pattern choices clearly, in your own words — repeatedly the actual differentiator, more than solving hard algorithms
Depth on whatever you name on your resume — interviewers are reported to circle back and ask "why" for specific technology choices
Software Engineer / Graduate Engineer Tr.notes: India reports (Bengaluru, Pune, Mumbai) show round counts from 2 to 4, and difficulty is consistently described as easy-to-moderate rather than hard.
